name: Olmec Civilization
summary: Flourished in the tropical lowlands of Veracruz and Tabasco. Carved 20-ton basalt Colossal Heads, pioneered the Mesoamerican rubber ballgame, ritual bloodletting, jade carving, the Long Count calendar, and the earliest writing in the Americas.
keyFacts: 17 monumental basalt Colossal Heads portraying Olmec rulers
Cascajal Block & Epi-Olmec script; concept of zero
Vulcanized rubber balls for the Mesoamerican ballgame

name: Maya Civilization
summary: Renowned for the only fully developed phonetic-logographic writing system in the pre-Columbian Americas, positional mathematics with an explicit zero, ultra-precise Venus and eclipse astronomy, and soaring limestone step-pyramids.
keyFacts: Maya hieroglyphic script and bark-paper codices (Dresden Codex)
Base-20 positional mathematics with zero & Long Count calendar
Tikal, Palenque, Copán, and Chichén Itzá astronomical architecture

name: Zapotecs & Teotihuacan
summary: Teotihuacan dominated Classic Mesoamerica with its Avenue of the Dead, Pyramid of the Sun, Pyramid of the Moon, multi-family apartment compounds, and obsidian export monopoly, while Zapotec Monte Albán ruled Oaxaca.
keyFacts: Pyramid of the Sun & Avenue of the Dead urban grid
Talud-tablero architectural style exported across Mesoamerica

name: Toltec Empire
summary: Postclassic central Mexican power famous for the Atlantean warrior columns at Tula and venerated by the later Aztecs as the supreme progenitors of civilization ("Toltecayotl").
keyFacts: Colossal basalt Atlantean warrior pillars at Tula

name: Aztec Empire (Triple Alliance)
summary: Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, and Tlacopan that built an island metropolis on Lake Texcoco connected by causeways, aqueducts, and hyper-productive chinampa "floating gardens."
keyFacts: Island metropolis of Tenochtitlan & Templo Mayor
Chinampa lacustrine agriculture supporting 200,000+ urban residents

name: New Spain → Mexico
summary: Hub of the Spanish Empire linking the Atlantic and Pacific (Manila Galleons), achieving independence in 1821 and undergoing the transformative Mexican Revolution (1910–1920).

Mexican Constitution of 1917 pioneering social and labor rights
